distinguishing_features: Active acoustic (HIFU) energy deposition to drive cavitation-mediated nucleation in droplet bulk, rather than passive foreign-nucleus collision.
Physically couples nucleation barrier to acoustic pressure amplitude computed from real-time static pressure and OAT.
Does not require consumable seeding agents (no AgI flares) — a hardware design change rather than monitoring or procedural capping.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reliably trigger ice nucleation in supercooled cloud droplets at marginal supercooling (above ~-5°C) where passive heterogeneous nucleation by conventional seeds is inefficient.
parsed.viable_reason: The physics is dubious as written: at 26.5 kPa, 50 kPa acoustic margin cannot overcome static pressure for sustained inertial cavitation, droplet residence in a 1 MHz focused field is far too short, and liquid droplets resist acoustic cavitation without nucleant gas nuclei, so the stated scale is implausible.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Using focused ultrasound cavitation to directly lower the bulk nucleation barrier at marginal supercooling is not a routine parameter tweak of any cited prior art and represents a genuinely non-obvious mechanism step.
